title: Tripoli vigil demanding government action on abducted intelligence official
location: Outside the Prime Minister's Council, Tripoli, Libya
scope: One local public vigil; no nationwide campaign boundary inferred.
organizer: Citizens; statement read by a group that named itself “Zintan Residents, Capital Residents”; exact organizing structure unclear.
threshold_50_evidence: unknown; the reviewed contemporary report describes protesters/vigil but provides no attendance count or explicit large-crowd characterization.

start_date.summary: Alwasat photo caption dates the vigil to 12 November 2024.

end_date.summary: No duration or end date reported; null/unknown.

location.summary: Article caption and body locate the vigil outside the Prime Minister's Council in Tripoli.

state_target.summary: Protesters demanded government action to disclose the whereabouts and secure the release of a kidnapped intelligence-security official, and criticized the government's failure to identify the abducting party.

demands.summary: Specific demand is government action/accountability in a kidnapping/disappearance case. No listed codebook category clearly fits; category list left empty rather than assigning an unsupported label.

organizer.summary: Article reports citizens and a statement by a group calling itself “Zintan Residents, Capital Residents”; independent organization details unknown.

participants_original.summary: No participant count published in the reviewed report.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No evidence in reviewed report that establishes at least 50 simultaneous participants; attendance unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: The reviewed passage does not establish violence by protesters; retain unknown.

state_response.summary: The report relays protesters' complaint that authorities had not announced a position before the vigil; it does not establish post-event response, arrests, dispersal, accommodation, killings or shootings.

notes: Single contemporary Alwasat report. An embedded Facebook media item was not opened; it is not counted as independent evidence. Exact threshold remains unproven. Native publication/access times and HTTP status are unavailable. The unit assignment does not contain original ccode; ccode left null rather than substituting an ISO value. Libya Witness query URL was also body-opened but redirected to an unassessed canonical same-domain path; the deviation is retained in its source card. Its wording closely resembles Alwasat and upstream relation is unresolved, so it is not used as independent corroboration or to promote this candidate. No turnout evidence.
